design_rationale: The paper explicitly reports a randomized, double-blinded placebo-controlled trial with a computer-generated list of random numbers used to allocate calcium or placebo treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated and concealed in opaque numbered envelopes/bottles, but a statistically significant baseline imbalance in maternal weight (p<0.01) plus non-significant imbalances in bacteriuria and chlamydial vaginitis raise some concern about the adequacy of the randomization in this small sample.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A computer-generated list of random numbers was used to allocate the corresponding treatments. Opaque envelopes with the bottles numbered were located at the clinic and the project coordinator was in charge of the administration of the treatment assigned." ... "The calcium group had lower mean maternal weight (63.0 ± 10.6 kg) than the placebo group (67.4 ± 13.5 kg; p < 0.01)."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome appears available for essentially all randomized women (94/95 vs 95/95), but denominators fluctuate across tables (N = 94, 91, 90, 89, 88, 87, 80) without a clear accounting of who is missing and why, so completeness cannot be fully verified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Three patients in the placebo group and four in the calcium group abandoned treatment at different times during the study and complete compliance information could not be obtained." ... "All participants (including one dropout until the time she left the study) are included."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, care providers and outcome assessors were blinded by an identical placebo, and an intention-to-treat analysis was used despite substantial but balanced non-compliance (~75% of tablets in both arms).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The placebo group received four tablets of the same weight, size, color, and organoleptic characteristics as the calcium tablets." ... "All subjects were included in the treatment group to which they were originally randomized regardless of any follow-up and treatment compliance experiences."

domain_judgments.rationale: Preterm delivery and birth weight are objective outcomes, gestational age was ascertained by a prespecified algorithm (LMP plus 16–20 week ultrasonography), and assessors were explicitly blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Gestational age was calculated using the best obstetric estimation by the attending obstetrician who was totally unaware of the treatment groups." ... "preterm labor without delivery, diagnosed by obstetricians unaware of the treatment group"

domain_judgments.rationale: A primary outcome and power calculation were prespecified, but no protocol/registration is available and the report includes numerous alternative outcome definitions (idiopathic, spontaneous, 30–37 weeks, vaginal deliveries only) and post hoc stratified/subgroup analyses, with at least one internally inconsistent p value (Apgar ≤7: 4.4% vs 10.5%, p = 0.004), suggesting flexible and possibly selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The a priori hypothesis that calcium supplementation reduces the incidence of prematurity (<37 weeks) is tested." ... "A stratified analysis was therefore performed by infection status."

overall_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled trial used computer-generated randomization with concealed allocation, blinded outcome assessment and intention-to-treat analysis (D2, D4 low), but there are some concerns from a significant baseline imbalance in maternal weight, inconsistent and unexplained denominators across outcome tables, and the absence of a pre-registered protocol alongside many alternative outcome definitions and post hoc subgroup analyses. No domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is 'some concerns'.

design_rationale: Participants were allocated to calcium or placebo using a computer-generated list of random numbers, with the list held by pharmacy personnel and clinicians blinded — explicit random allocation in a double-blind trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated random number list was used, the list was concealed with pharmacy personnel who dispensed matching placebo, and baseline characteristics (age, gestational age, BP, proteinuria, uric acid, platelets) were similar between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "patients were assigned using a computer-generated list of random numbers... The randomization list was maintained by pharmacy personnel; the drugs and placebo were delivered by the pharmacy to the antepartum ward"

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blinding with matching placebo and a standardized inpatient management protocol makes performance bias unlikely, but the paper reports no information on adherence/compliance with tablets, no co-intervention monitoring beyond general statements, and does not state whether an intention-to-treat analysis was used (though analysed numbers equal randomized numbers, which is reassuring).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Clinicians caring for study patients were blinded to treatment group allocation." ... "Clinical management, which followed an established routine for preeclampsia, included hospitalization, bed rest, serial measurements of BP, and daily weighing."

domain_judgments.rationale: All 75 randomized women (36 calcium, 39 placebo) appear in the outcome tables with no reported withdrawals or losses, and as hospitalized inpatients followed to delivery essentially complete outcome ascertainment is plausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Severe preeclampsia led to preterm delivery in 18 of 36 (50%, 95% CI 33–67) patients in the calcium group and in 19 of 39 (48.7%, 95% CI 32–65) in the placebo group"

domain_judgments.rationale: Progression to severe preeclampsia was defined by explicit, objective pre-specified criteria (BP thresholds, proteinuria, platelets, liver enzymes) applied consistently in both arms, and assessing clinicians were blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Diagnostic criteria and clinical management for severe preeclampsia were applied consistently." ... "Clinicians caring for study patients were blinded to treatment group allocation."

domain_judgments.rationale: An a priori hypothesis, primary outcome and power calculation are stated and many outcomes are reported, but there is no protocol/registration available for verification and the trial was stopped early (before reaching the planned sample size) for funding reasons, with no pre-specified stopping rule described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Because of a decline in perinatal research support, the study was terminated three cases earlier than suggested by power analysis."

overall_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled trial had a sound computer-generated randomization with pharmacy-held allocation, balanced baseline characteristics, complete outcome data, and objectively defined, blinded outcome assessment. Overall judgment of "some concerns" is driven by unreported adherence/analysis-population details (D2) and the absence of a registered protocol combined with early termination for funding reasons (D5); the trial was also slightly underpowered.

design_rationale: Explicit double-blind placebo-controlled RCT: "The women were assigned randomly in a double blind fashion at 20 weeks' gestation to 1 of 2 treatment groups (calcium/placebo) using computer generated random number table."

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated random sequence was used and baseline characteristics were well balanced, but no details are given on allocation concealment (e.g., sequentially numbered identical containers or who held the list), leaving concealment uncertain.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The women were assigned randomly in a double blind fashion at 20 weeks' gestation to 1 of 2 treatment groups (calcium/placebo) using computer generated random number table.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and care providers were blinded via identical placebo, compliance was similar across groups (82% vs 88%), and an intention-to-treat analysis was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The placebo group received 4 tablets of the same size, weight and colour as the calcium tablets. ... All randomized patients were included in the treatment group to which they had been originally assigned regardless of compliance or gestational age at delivery.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was small (5.5%) and balanced between arms, and the effect size is large enough that such attrition is unlikely to explain the result; however, reasons for loss were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eleven women (5.47%) were lost to follow-up after randomization (5 in the placebo group and 6 in the calcium group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes (BP thresholds, 24-h proteinuria) were objectively and uniformly defined, measured identically in both groups with a random-zero sphygmomanometer by a single trained physician under double-blind conditions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At each visit blood pressure values were measured with patient seated after 10 minutes of rest by one physician (SD) specially trained and recruited for this study using random zero sphygmomanometer.

domain_judgments.rationale: A pre-specified primary endpoint and a priori sample-size calculation are reported, but there is no accessible protocol/registration and multiple secondary outcomes and subdivisions of PIH are reported, so selective reporting cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The main end point of the trial was the development of PIH.

overall_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT had sound blinding, objective outcome measurement, minimal balanced attrition and an ITT analysis, but allocation concealment procedures were not described and no protocol/pre-registration is available to rule out selective reporting. Overall risk is therefore "some concerns", driven by domains 1 and 5.

design_rationale: Explicit random allocation of 106 nulliparous women to calcium or placebo using a table of random numbers in a double-blind placebo-controlled trial ("Using a table of random numbers each patient was assigned independently in sequence to one of two treatment regimens").

domain_judgments.rationale: A random number table was used and tablets/containers were identical, but allocation concealment is not explicitly described, and baseline systolic (106.4 vs 103.2), diastolic (P=0.07) and ionized calcium (P=0.07) values were consistently higher in the placebo group, with authors themselves adjusting "as a precaution against imperfect randomization".
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Using a table of random numbers each patient was assigned independently in sequence to one of two treatment regimens. ... The mean serum ionized calcium level at the pretreatment assessment (week 24) was slightly higher in the placebo group ... (P=0·07)

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and clinical staff were blinded with an indistinguishable placebo, compliance was monitored by pill counts and home visits, and no deviations or co-interventions beyond standard prenatal care were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment assignment was double blind, with the composition of the tablets unknown to the patients and to all clinical personnel involved in the study. ... Patient compliance with the treatment protocol was assessed during each prenatal visit by counting the number of tablets remaining in the container and by random unscheduled home visits by the investigators.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes (PIH by standard criteria, blood pressure, serum ionized calcium) were objectively and uniformly measured with a standardized, calibrated protocol by a blinded assessor, though use of a single unblinded-to-trial-hypothesis observer and no explicit digit-preference control is a minor residual concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All blood pressures were measured by the same investigator (M.N.) with a mercury sphygomanometer ... which was calibrated by the Instituto Ecuatoriano de Normalización y Medidas, Quito.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 106 randomized women completed the study and PIH incidence appears to be based on near-complete follow-up, but 14/106 (13%) were excluded from the blood pressure/calcium analyses for delivering before 38 weeks — a post-randomization, outcome-related exclusion that is only partially justified (authors state none had signs of PIH).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Only women with no missing values for any of the covariate and outcome variables were included in these statistical analyses, 49 in the calcium-supplemented group and 43 in the placebo group. Six women in the calcium-supplemented group and eight in the placebo group were eliminated from analysis because they were delivered before 38 weeks

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registered protocol or pre-specified analysis plan is available, the power calculation appears to be constructed post hoc from the achieved sample size with a one-tailed alpha, and multiple outcomes/analyses (PIH, SBP, DBP, calcium, subgroup comparisons) are reported without correction.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: With the sample size obtained, employing a one-tailed alpha of 0·05 and a minimum power of 0·8, this sets a requirement that PIH risk be reduced to approximately ≤7·5% in the treatment group

overall_summary: This double-blind placebo-controlled trial had robust blinding and objective, standardized outcome measurement, but concerns remain regarding unreported allocation concealment with consistent baseline imbalances favouring the calcium group, post-randomization exclusion of 13% of participants from the blood pressure analyses, and absence of a pre-specified protocol/analysis plan with an apparently post hoc one-tailed power calculation. No single domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is "some concerns".

design_rationale: Explicitly a "multicentre, randomized controlled double-blind trial" with central telephone randomization to calcium (1.8 g/day) or identical lactose placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central telephone randomization with a drug-company-prepared schedule stratified by centre using variable blocks and sealed identical treatment packs ensured concealment; baseline characteristics were similar between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Women who gave consent were enrolled into the trial by telephoning the central randomization number... The randomization schedule was prepared by the drug company with stratification made by centre using variable blocks."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and care providers were blinded by identical placebo tablets; although substantial numbers stopped medication (31% calcium vs 24% placebo), all primary analyses were intention-to-treat on the allocated group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All primary analyses were based on the treatment group allocated at randomization (intention-to-treat)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for all 456 randomized women and their babies, with no attrition for primary outcomes (dietary calcium covariate data were incomplete but this concerns adjustment, not outcome ascertainment).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Study outcome data were available for all 456 women and their babies."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes used standard international definitions and objective measures (blood pressure, proteinuria, gestational age), with data collectors, the checking obstetrician and analysts blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Delivery and postnatal care details were collected from case notes by the research assistants following hospital discharge and checked by a senior obstetrician, all blinded to treatment allocation."

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary outcomes were prespecified and reported, but the trial was stopped early at 48% of the target sample size with analyses done after unblinding, no adjustment for multiple comparisons, and both unadjusted and several differently adjusted models reported, so selective emphasis of the significant results cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "No adjustments were made for multiple comparisons." / "Recruitment to the trial was stopped by the steering group without knowledge of study outcomes after 456 women were randomized when the limited financial resources available for the trial were exhausted."

overall_summary: Well-conducted double-blind placebo-controlled trial with concealed central randomization, complete outcome data, objective blinded outcome assessment and intention-to-treat analysis. Overall "some concerns" driven by D5: early termination at 48% of the planned sample size, multiple outcomes/adjusted models without correction for multiplicity, raising the possibility of selective reporting and inflated effect estimates.

design_rationale: Explicit computer-generated random allocation: "Randomization lists for each site were produced with computer-generated random number blocking (SAS Institute, Inc, Cary, NC) with randomly varying groups of 6 to 8 women," in a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 8325 women.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central, computer-generated, country-stratified block randomization performed off-site by the WHO Clinical Trials Unit with codes withheld until analysis and allocation concealed via identical consecutively numbered treatment boxes; baseline characteristics were well balanced across the two arms of 4151 vs 4161 women.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomization was performed independently for each study site by the Clinical Trials Unit at WHO/HRP Geneva, Switzerland, and transmitted only to the labeling and packaging company... Randomization codes remained at the WHO Clinical Trial Unit until the time of analysis and were not available to any person until the analyses were completed."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and staff were blinded by matched placebo tablets identical in form, colour and taste; compliance (85% vs 86%) and reasons for stopping treatment were similar between arms, and analysis followed the intention-to-treat principle with all randomized subjects included irrespective of compliance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Data from all subjects were included, irrespective of compliance or follow-up failures (intention-to-treat principle)"; "The chewable tablets ... contained calcium carbonate or placebo ... They were identical in form, color, and taste."

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was small and near-identical between arms (3.4% calcium vs 3.7% placebo for delivery data), hospital records were sought for those lost, and the magnitude of missingness is too small and too balanced to plausibly bias the effect estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Delivery information was unavailable for 143 women (3.4%) in the calcium group and 155 women (3.7%) in the placebo group; therefore, they did not contribute to the preterm analyses, but the available data were included in the analyses for other outcomes."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective, pre-defined clinical events (blood pressure thresholds, proteinuria, eclampsia, preterm delivery, death) measured with standardized, calibrated equipment and WHO-certified trained staff who were blinded to allocation, so assessment could not have been differentially influenced; the only caveat is a minor protocol change in the severe-preeclampsia interval (6 to 4 hours) made during the pilot and applied identically to both arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Blood pressure was recorded with a mercury sphygmomanometer after 2 measurements (the average was used) at 3-minute intervals... Principal investigators and nurse-coordinators were certified by WHO (Geneva) in a course..."

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the authors state all outcomes and subgroup analyses were protocol-specified and all endpoints reported, the headline positive findings derive from numerous secondary outcomes and two composite indices — one of which ("severe maternal morbidity and mortality index") was explicitly developed after protocol inception on a Data Monitoring Committee recommendation — plus an age-stratified subgroup effect with a non-significant interaction, creating multiplicity and selective-emphasis concerns on a trial whose primary outcomes were both null.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A second summary indicator, the 'severe maternal morbidity and mortality index' was developed to further evaluate treatment effects on major maternal complications on the basis of criteria that were used for analyzing outcomes in the published Cochrane Systematic Review and a recommendation of the Data Monitoring Committee of the trial."

overall_summary: This large multicentre WHO trial is methodologically strong for its primary outcomes — central computer-generated concealed randomization, balanced baselines, genuine double-blinding with identical placebo, ~85% compliance, <4% balanced attrition, standardized objective outcome ascertainment, and ITT analysis (all D1–D4 low). Overall judgment is "some concerns" because the reported benefits rest on numerous secondary outcomes and composite indices, one of which was constructed after protocol inception, and on a subgroup analysis with a non-significant interaction, while both pre-specified primary outcomes (preeclampsia and preterm delivery) were null.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in which primigravidas were "randomly assigned... to receive 2 g of elemental calcium or placebo" using a "simple randomization sequence developed manually" with coded, identical-looking tablet packets.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was concealed via coded identical packets and baseline characteristics were well balanced, but the sequence was "developed manually" with no description of the random number source, and the group sizes are notably unequal (290 vs 262), raising mild concerns about the sequence generation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The blinding of study participants and investigators was done by assigning coded numbers to the packets, each containing 60 tablets of calcium or placebo, according to a simple randomization sequence developed manually. The packets were then distributed to the participants using the random numbers in sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and investigators were blinded by identical placebo tablets and the code was disclosed only after study completion, but compliance was only ~78–80% and analysis was restricted to completers rather than intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Compliance with medication was 78% in the calcium group and 80% in the placebo group. ... Further data analysis was performed for those who completed the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: About 5–6% of randomized women lacked outcome data (17 calcium, 11 placebo) with no stated reasons for loss, no sensitivity/ITT analysis, and the recruitment numbers are inconsistently reported (602 vs 552), though the proportion missing is modest and similar between arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 552 women recruited for the study, 290 were randomly assigned to the calcium group and 262 to the placebo group. However, data regarding delivery and neonatal outcome could be obtained for 273 women in the calcium group and 251 women in the placebo group

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes (pre-eclampsia, blood pressure, preterm delivery, birth weight) were objectively defined using standard criteria and measured identically in both arms by assessors blinded to allocation, although proteinuria was only assessed qualitatively by dipstick.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Blood pressure was measured at each visit using a manual mercury sphygmomanometer... Pre-eclampsia was defined as a systolic blood pressure higher than 140 mm Hg and a diastolic blood pressure higher than 90 mm Hg on 2 occasions at least 4 hours apart after 20 weeks of pregnancy... along with proteinuria

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-specified analysis plan is reported, multiple outcomes and post hoc median-split subgroup analyses are presented, and the sample-size/power statement appears to be computed from the observed event rates, raising concerns about selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Further analysis was done to evaluate the role of baseline urinary calcium and baseline dietary calcium intake on the development of pre-eclampsia. The participants were divided into low or high urinary calcium subgroups depending on whether the 24-hour urinary calcium excretion was greater or less than the median value

overall_summary: This double-blind placebo-controlled trial had adequate blinding and objective, consistently measured outcomes, but concerns remain about the manually generated randomization sequence with unequal arms, completers-only (non-ITT) analysis with ~78–80% compliance and ~5% unexplained attrition, and the absence of pre-registration alongside post hoc subgroup analyses. No single domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is 'some concerns'.

design_rationale: Explicit multicenter, double-blind, randomized placebo-controlled trial: "They were randomized at each hospital by a random-sample generator program provided by the Epistat Statistical Package," with sealed opaque numbered envelopes for allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Sequence was computer-generated and allocation was concealed in numbered, sealed, opaque envelopes held at each site with codes kept centrally; baseline characteristics were closely balanced apart from small differences in previous abortions and smoking that are consistent with chance (and were explicitly discussed with reference to Altman & Doré).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "They were randomized at each hospital by a random-sample generator program provided by the Epistat Statistical Package. A complete set of numbered, sealed, opaque envelopes containing the randomization codes was sent to each of the three hospitals."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, nurses and physicians were blinded with placebo tablets identical in weight, size, flavour and colour; compliance was comparable between arms (86% vs 84% of tablets) and an intention-to-treat analysis was used regardless of noncompliance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Thus, the woman, the nurses, and the physicians responsible for prenatal care were all unaware of the woman's treatment status." ... "All women were included in the treatment group to which they had been assigned, regardless of any problems that occurred during follow-up or as a consequence of noncompliance with treatment."

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 27/1194 (2.3%) were lost immediately after randomization (balanced, 13 vs 14) and a sensitivity analysis including them gave very similar results; the further incomplete follow-up (46 placebo vs 52 calcium) was balanced, handled by censoring in life-table analysis, and due to reasons (hospital/residence change) unlikely to relate to outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Twenty-seven women (2.3 percent) were lost to follow-up after randomization (13 in the placebo group and 14 in the calcium group)... The results were very similar when the 27 women who were lost to follow-up immediately after randomization were included in the analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes used standard objective criteria (BP ≥140/90 on two occasions ≥6 h apart plus proteinuria >0.3 g/L), measured identically in both arms with calibrated random-zero sphygmomanometers, repeat-measurement validation and staff retraining, and assessors were blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Blood pressures were measured with four random-zero sphygmomanometers rotated monthly among the centers and calibrated every three weeks."

domain_judgments.rationale: The a priori primary endpoint and hypothesis were pre-specified in a prior publication, but there is no accessible protocol/registration, diastolic BP was defined by two alternative Korotkoff phases with only phase 5 results presented, and multiple subgroup (urinary calcium:creatinine strata) and secondary analyses were reported, leaving some scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Although the rates of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy were calculated with use of both phase 4 and phase 5 Korotkoff sounds for diastolic blood pressure, the results based on the phase 5 sound are presented"

overall_summary: This is a well-conducted double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with computer-generated allocation, concealed opaque envelopes, balanced baseline characteristics, minimal and balanced attrition, ITT analysis, and objective blinded outcome ascertainment. The overall rating of "some concerns" is driven solely by Domain 5: no protocol/registration is available, only one of two pre-specified diastolic BP definitions (phase 5 Korotkoff) is reported, and numerous subgroup and secondary analyses are presented, allowing some possibility of selective reporting.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomly assigned: "We randomly assigned 4589 healthy nulliparous women ... to receive daily treatment with either 2 g of elemental calcium or placebo", using a "computer-generated simple randomization sequence developed by the study statisticians."

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated random sequence implemented via sequentially numbered, identical blister packs prepared by the manufacturer (concealed allocation), and baseline characteristics were closely balanced across the two arms of ~2295 each.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Packages of study tablets were prepared and numbered by the pharmaceutical manufacturer according to a computer-generated simple randomization sequence developed by the study statisticians... On enrollment, each woman was assigned the next numbered package of medication at that center."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind placebo-controlled design with matched chewable tablets and outcome assessors unaware of assignment; although mean compliance was modest (64% vs 67%), the primary analysis was intention-to-treat including all randomized women.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All the women randomly assigned to treatment were included in the primary analysis regardless of their follow-up status or compliance with treatment."

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was small (5.5%) and nearly identical between arms (132 calcium vs 121 placebo), making bias from missingness unlikely for the ~7% event-rate outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Two hundred fifty-three women (5.5 percent) were lost to follow-up: 132 in the calcium group and 121 in the placebo group."

domain_judgments.rationale: Preeclampsia was defined a priori with objective standardized blood-pressure and proteinuria criteria, measured identically in both arms by certified examiners blinded to allocation; only the non-systematically surveyed neonatal hypocalcemia outcome is weaker.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Surveillance for preeclampsia was conducted by personnel unaware of treatment-group assignments, using standardized measurements of blood pressure and urinary protein excretion at uniformly scheduled prenatal visits"

domain_judgments.rationale: The rationale, design, methods and outcome definitions were published in advance (Control Clin Trials 1996), the primary outcome and prespecified subgroup/interaction analyses (dietary calcium, urinary calcium, age, compliance) are all reported including null findings, with an independent DSMB overseeing the trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A detailed description of the screening and selection procedures, including a complete list of exclusion criteria, has been published previously." / "Levine RJ, Esterlitz JR, Raymond EG, et al. Trial of Calcium for Preeclampsia Prevention (CPEP): rationale, design, and methods."

overall_summary: This large multicenter double-blind placebo-controlled trial used computer-generated randomization with concealed, sequentially numbered identical medication packs, blinded standardized objective outcome ascertainment, minimal and balanced loss to follow-up (5.5%), intention-to-treat analysis, and a pre-published protocol, so all five RoB 2 domains are low risk. The only minor caveats—modest medication compliance (~64–67%) and non-systematic surveillance of the secondary neonatal hypocalcemia outcome—do not affect the intention-to-treat estimate for the primary preeclampsia outcome.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly reports a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with allocation by a computer-generated list: "Women with positive angiotensin sensitivity tests were enrolled in the study and randomized by means of a computer-generated list (Systat 5.0)".

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was by a computer-generated list with identical matched placebo dispensed by the hospital pharmacy in serially numbered bottles (implying concealment), and baseline characteristics were comparable between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "randomized by means of a computer-generated list (Systat 5.0; Systat Intelligent Software, Evanston, IL) to receive either 2 g/day of elemental calcium or matching placebo... The tablets were dispensed by the hospital pharmacy in serially numbered computerized pill bottles"

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blinding with identical placebo and a stated intention-to-treat principle, but compliance was only ~80% and four randomized calcium patients were excluded from analysis, so the analysis was not fully ITT.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All randomized patients were included in the treatment group to which they had been originally assigned regardless of compliance." / "four were excluded from the analysis after randomization because of lack of information"

domain_judgments.rationale: Four of 33 randomized calcium participants (12%) were excluded for missing data with no losses in the placebo group — differential missingness in a small trial — although sensitivity analyses suggested the conclusions for pregnancy-induced hypertension were robust (the worst-case preeclampsia analysis became non-significant, P = .12).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Four additional women, assigned to the calcium group, were completely lost to follow-up and could not be included in the follow-up analyses." / "Even if each of these four patients developed preeclampsia, eight of 33 patients (24.2%) receiving calcium versus 15 of 34 (44.1%) receiving placebo would have developed preeclampsia (P = .12)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes used objective, pre-specified BP and proteinuria criteria, were collected before unblinding, and charts were adjudicated by two perinatologists blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Outcome data were collected after delivery but before the code was broken... all charts were reviewed by two perinatologists blinded to group allocation."

domain_judgments.rationale: An a priori hypothesis, sample-size calculation, and named primary outcome are reported, but there is no trial registration or accessible protocol and multiple outcome operationalizations (preeclampsia, gestational hypertension, composite PIH, perinatal outcomes) were analyzed, so selective reporting cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The a priori hypothesis was that oral calcium supplementation would reduce the incidence of pregnancy-induced hypertension from 60% in angiotensin II-sensitive nulliparas to 20%."

overall_summary: Randomization and blinded outcome assessment were well executed, but differential post-randomization exclusion of four calcium-group participants (with the worst-case preeclampsia analysis losing significance), imperfect adherence to intention-to-treat, and absence of a registered protocol raise some concerns. No domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is "some concerns".

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial using a computer-generated random number table with block randomization: "study patients were assigned in a double-blind fashion to receive orally either 1.5 g elemental calcium as calcium carbonate or placebo daily, using a randomization schedule in blocks of ten developed by a computer-generated random number table."

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated random number table with blocks of ten was used, allocation was concealed through an independent Investigational Drug Pharmacy preparing identical-appearing containers/tablets, and baseline demographic and laboratory characteristics did not differ between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "using a randomization schedule in blocks of ten developed by a computer-generated random number table (Excel version 6.0...). All containers and tablets were prepared and dispensed by the University of Washington Investigational Drug Pharmacy."

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of participants and personnel was secured with matched placebo, but the analysis was not intention-to-treat — noncompliant subjects were explicitly excluded from analysis and five of 23 randomized women (including a discontinuation for side effects) were dropped, leaving an as-treated/per-protocol analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Noncompliance was defined as missing 2 consecutive days of prescribed study drug ... and noncompliant subjects were excluded from analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Five of 23 randomized women (22%) did not complete, with highly imbalanced attrition (4 of 11 placebo vs 1 of 12 calcium), leaving only 7 placebo subjects for hemodynamic analysis; the authors themselves concede an effect may have gone undetected due to attrition and no sensitivity or imputation analysis was performed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Twenty-three women were randomized, and 18 of them completed the study. Of the five who failed to complete the study, three developed preterm labor and were treated with terbutaline (all placebo), one was noncompliant (placebo), and one self-discontinued study medication due to side effects (calcium)." ... "it is possible that an effect is present but went undetected due to study subject attrition."

domain_judgments.rationale: Cardiac output was measured with a previously validated Doppler technique under standardized conditions (left lateral recumbent, 5 minutes rest) and blood pressure by automated cuff, applied identically in both arms of a double-blind trial, so assessor knowledge of allocation could not plausibly influence these largely objective measures.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Cardiac output was measured by Doppler technique using the UltraCOM Cardiac Output Monitor ... as described previously. Blood pressure and hemodynamic measurements were performed in the left lateral recumbent position after 5 minutes of rest."

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registered protocol or analysis plan is referenced (consistent with the 1997 era), and although cardiac output is clearly pre-specified as the primary outcome via the power calculation, multiple additional outcomes (MAP, TPR, SV, HR, calcium levels, obstetric outcomes) and multiple analytic approaches (within-group over time, between-group at 2 hours and 6 weeks) were reported without correction, allowing some scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Assuming a mean cardiac output of 6.2 ± 1.0 L/minute, sample size calculation indicated the need to study 20 subjects to detect a 20% (1.2 L/minute) difference in cardiac output between calcium- and placebo-treated subjects (α = .05, β = .8)."

overall_summary: Although the randomization procedure, blinding, and outcome measurement were sound, the trial is at high risk of bias overall because of substantial and differentially distributed attrition (5/23 randomized, with 4 of 5 dropouts from the placebo arm, leaving only 7 placebo participants) combined with a per-protocol analysis that excluded noncompliant subjects. These losses left the already small trial underpowered relative to its own sample-size calculation, so the null finding for cardiac output cannot be confidently attributed to absence of effect.
